knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson requires the method to match the authorised site scope and current product labels, with no uncontrolled hazard remaining. It also says cleaners should not diagnose disease or assume every stain is infectious.

Unknown biological hazards are stopped and escalated through the site process, under the site infection-prevention plan, rather than judged or cleaned up by the worker. The worker does not decide whether a hazard is infectious and carry on.
The instruction says infection hazards can be transferred through hands, contaminated tools, touch surfaces, droplets or other pathways.

practicalCriteria: Follows the authorised sequence and site procedures
Uses suitable tools, product instructions and contamination controls
Recognises and escalates unsafe or out-of-scope conditions
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record covering procedure steps 1-8
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 2 is not done: Follow the site infection-prevention plan, and escalate any unknown biological hazard or outbreak-specific requirement.
Stop work if procedure step 6 is not done: Do not wipe a clean surface, such as a door handle, with a cloth that has just touched a toilet flush plate.
Stop work if procedure step 7 is not done: Do not diagnose disease or assume that a stain is infectious; stop and escalate when a hazard is uncontrolled.
